title: Bits That Strictly Alternate
statement: You get a positive integer n. Write it in binary without leading zeros. Return true if every pair of neighbouring bits differs, so the bits go 1, 0, 1, 0, … all the way down. Otherwise return false.

examples.why: 42 is 101010 in binary. Every neighbour pair differs.
11 is 1011. The last two bits are both 1.
9 is 1001. No two 1s touch, but the two 0s in the middle do. Checking only for adjacent 1s is not enough.

hints: Walk the bits from the lowest one up. What should each bit be compared with?
Shift n right by one: it lines every bit up with its left neighbour. What does XOR of n and n >> 1 look like when the bits alternate?
For alternating bits, x = n XOR (n >> 1) is all ones, like 0b1111. A number of all ones plus 1 is a power of two, so x & (x + 1) is 0.

explain.intuition:
The direct way reads the bits one at a time from the low end: remember the previous bit, and fail as soon as the next one is the same. That is O(number of bits), at most 31 steps.

The bit trick compares all neighbours at once. n >> 1 moves every bit one place right, so bit i of n ^ (n >> 1) is 1 exactly when bits i and i + 1 of n differ. If the bits alternate, every position below the top one differs, and x = n ^ (n >> 1) is a solid block of ones like 111111. A solid block of ones is one less than a power of two, so adding 1 carries through every bit and x & (x + 1) is 0.
steps: If the bits of n alternate, x is all ones from bit 0 up to the top bit of n.
pitfalls: Checking only n & (n >> 1) === 0. That rules out adjacent 1s but not adjacent 0s, so 9 (1001) passes by mistake.
Comparing with a fixed pattern like 0x55555555. Alternating numbers can start with either 10… or 101…, and their length varies.
In JavaScript, x + 1 can reach 2³¹, which becomes negative in 32-bit bit operations. The result is still right here, but use >>> and keep values in range to be safe.

solutions.title: Read bits one by one
solutions.idea: Peel off the lowest bit each step and compare it with the previous one.

solutions.title: XOR with itself shifted
solutions.idea: n ^ (n >> 1) is all ones exactly when neighbouring bits always differ; all ones plus 1 shares no bit with itself.
